# reader — the demo, at 1280x820, driven entirely from the keyboard.
#
# Every book in it was generated by this program or exported by another app in
# this repository. Nothing of the user's is opened, named or shown.
#
# The pointer is not used: the recorder reports that pointer steps do not reach
# the client on this seat. That is no loss here — the application is meant to
# be usable without a mouse, and this is the proof.
#
#   PALMY_READER_HOME=$PWD/apps/reader/demo/state \
#     bash apps/tools/headless-record.sh apps/reader/reader.bin \
#       apps/reader/demo.mp4 apps/reader/demo.txt 1280 820

wait 1.6

# --- the library: six books, their covers, formats and authors
key Right
wait 0.6
key Right
wait 0.5
key Right
wait 0.5
key Right
wait 0.5
key Right
wait 0.8
key Home
wait 1.0

# open the large EPUB
key Home
key Return
wait 2.0

# --- turning pages
key Right
wait 1.0
key Right
wait 1.0
key Right
wait 1.0
key Left
wait 1.2

# --- the type size, and the text reflowing to it
key plus
wait 0.8
key plus
wait 0.8
key plus
wait 1.5
key minus
wait 0.7
key minus
wait 1.4

# --- the three themes
key 2
wait 1.5
key 3
wait 1.5
key 1
wait 1.0

# --- justified instead of ragged right
key u
wait 1.6
key u
wait 1.0

# --- search within the book
key slash
wait 0.9
type Gutenberg
wait 1.8
key Return
wait 1.5
key Return
wait 1.5
key Down
wait 1.5
key Escape
wait 1.0

# --- the table of contents, and a jump from it
key t
wait 1.4
key Down
wait 0.4
key Down
wait 0.4
key Down
wait 0.4
key Down
wait 0.4
key Down
wait 0.8
key Return
wait 2.0

# --- continuous scroll instead of pages
key m
wait 1.5
key Down
key Down
key Down
key Down
key Down
wait 1.4
key m
wait 1.2

# --- a bookmark, and the list of them
key b
wait 1.2
key l
wait 1.8
key Escape
wait 0.9

# --- the reading settings
key s
wait 2.0
key Escape
wait 0.9

# --- back to the library, which now knows how far into each book you are
key g
wait 2.0

# reopening returns to the page it was left on. That is the whole reason a
# position is a chapter and a byte offset rather than a page number: a page
# number means nothing once the type size has changed under it.
# `key Home` twice on purpose: the recorder drops an invocation's first
# keystroke now and then, and Home in the library is idempotent, so it makes a
# safe throwaway before a press that must land.
key Home
wait 0.8
key Return
wait 1.2
# Space opens the selected book too. Both are sent because the recorder
# batches the whole steps file into one wtype invocation and a key late in a
# long batch is occasionally not delivered; if Return landed, this turns a
# page, which is harmless and visibly true.
key space
wait 2.6

# --- and into a fixed-page document, which is a different thing to read
key g
wait 1.7
key Home
key Right
key Right
key Right
key Right
wait 1.2
key End
key Left
key Left
wait 1.0
key Return
wait 2.4

# a PDF has no type size: it has fit and zoom
key f
wait 1.6
key plus
wait 1.6
key w
wait 1.6

# turning pages through a rasterised document
key Right
wait 1.6
key Right
wait 1.7

# its outline, read out of the PDF's own bookmarks
key t
wait 1.6
key Down
wait 0.4
key Down
wait 0.4
key Down
wait 0.6
key Return
wait 2.6
